prompt: An online poll about internet use finds that almost everyone is online.
tells: An online poll about internet use
trap: The sample might be big; it's still skewed.

prompt: A gym surveys its members and concludes that most adults exercise daily.
trap: Size isn't the problem; who was asked is.

prompt: Product reviews come mostly from very happy or very angry customers.
tells: mostly from very happy or very angry
why: Who chose to answer biases the sample.
trap: It's about who answered, not the shape of the data.

prompt: A study of successful companies' habits ignores the companies that failed.
trap: No third factor; the sample left out the failures.

prompt: A phone survey run during work hours reaches mostly retirees.
trap: The number of calls isn't the issue.

prompt: A professor asks only students who came to office hours how the course is going.
tells: only students who came to office hours
trap: Who was asked matters more than how many.
